answer: Each agent works one basalt column in a tidal quarry, cutting a spiral groove one turn deeper every epoch and setting a pearl bead into the groove as a dated marker. A traveling inspector gauges the groove and counts the beads against the quarry ledger; a shallow cut or a bead out of sequence loses the face for a season. The tide washes the column twice a day, so a groove cut in a hurry shows fresh dust the next morning. Faking a thousand agents means cutting a thousand spirals by hand and buying a thousand pearls, one quarry face per fake name.
